approvalRequirements: The project must qualify as a new or expanding renewable-energy facility eligible for a Chapter 9B tax abatement.
The applicant must submit the prescribed abatement application and petition to an authorized city, county, or public industrial authority.
The local granting authority must adopt the required resolution and execute an abatement agreement before the property is placed in service.
The project must complete required state and local tax filings, reporting, and continuing compliance obligations.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: A qualifying facility can receive the abatement, but the authorized local granting authority has discretion over whether to approve the request and its terms.
reviews.evidenceText: Chapter 9B abatements are granted by an authorized city, county, or public industrial authority through a local resolution and abatement agreement.

approvalRequirements: The renewable-energy system must satisfy the current statutory technology and property requirements.
The municipality must have adopted an ordinance granting the exemption for the applicable system class.
The owner must submit the information and supporting records required by the municipality or local tax assessor, including system and installation documentation.
For a commercial system, the owner must provide the applicable interconnection and program-enrollment records required by state regulation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The state authorizes the exemption, but the benefit exists only in a municipality that adopted it and remains subject to local assessor verification.
reviews.evidenceText: Rhode Island law permits municipalities to exempt qualifying renewable-energy systems by ordinance, with local documentation and assessor review required.

approvalRequirements: The property must fit the legacy local-option commercial or industrial renewable-energy provision, including the applicable statutory installation-date window.
The system must meet the applicable use, capacity, and technology requirements in the current statute.
The municipality's legislative body must have adopted the authorized abatement for the covered property.
The owner must file the applicable annual exemption application with the local assessor by the statutory deadline and provide supporting documentation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current local-option provision is limited to covered commercial or industrial systems installed during a historical statutory window, so a new 2026 project generally cannot qualify under this legacy route.
reviews.evidenceText: Connecticut's current statute preserves a local-option abatement for covered commercial or industrial systems installed during the 2010 through 2013 statutory window and requires assessor filings.

approvalRequirements: The property must be located in a municipality that has established an eligible clean-energy assessment district and application process.
The proposed improvement must qualify under the current Nebraska clean-energy assessment statutes.
The owner must submit the municipal application and establish that property taxes, assessments, liens, and relevant debts are not delinquent or in default.
The project must satisfy the municipality's financial-resource and project-economics review, including any applicable savings-to-principal requirement or authorized waiver.
Each prior mortgage holder must provide the consent or subordination required by statute for the property type.
The owner, municipality, and financing parties must execute the project and assessment contracts, followed by required completion verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Financing is available only in an adopting municipality and remains contingent on property eligibility, financial review, lienholder consent, project economics, and execution of the assessment contract.
reviews.evidenceText: Nebraska municipalities may create clean-energy assessment districts and review applications, financial condition, project economics, mortgage-holder consent, and assessment contracts before financing.

approvalRequirements: The county, city, town, village, or school district must have adopted the exemption by local law or resolution after the required hearing.
The project must be qualifying new construction or a substantial reconstruction, alteration, or improvement rather than ordinary maintenance or repair.
The project must meet the applicable construction-date, cost, permit, and certificate-of-occupancy requirements.
The building must obtain LEED certification or another locally accepted equivalent green-building certification at an eligible level.
The owner must file the prescribed exemption application and certification records with the local assessor.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The exemption is noncompetitive for a qualifying certified building, but it is available only where the local taxing jurisdiction adopted it and the assessor validates the project and certification.
reviews.evidenceText: New York's green-building exemption applies only after local adoption and requires qualifying construction, recognized green-building certification, and an assessor application.

approvalRequirements: The property must be in a New Mexico county or other jurisdiction that has opted into the current C-PACE program.
The property and project must meet the current commercial, industrial, agricultural, nonprofit, or qualifying multifamily eligibility rules.
The owner must submit the required project, ownership, cost, technical, and financing information to the statewide program administrator.
The administrator must certify program eligibility, and the project must pass private-capital underwriting and any required technical review.
The owner must obtain required mortgage-holder or other secured-party consents and execute the financing and special-assessment documents before funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current successor C-PACE pathway is available only in opted-in jurisdictions and requires administrator certification, private underwriting, secured-party consent, and financing close.
reviews.evidenceText: New Mexico C-PACE operates in opted-in jurisdictions, with statewide eligibility certification followed by private financing and a special property assessment.

approvalRequirements: The solar equipment must meet the current statutory definition and applicable residential size, use, and installation conditions.
For the local-option route, the locality must have adopted the authorized exemption ordinance; any applicable statewide small-system route must independently meet its statutory conditions.
The owner must apply to the local building department or other designated local official for certification of the qualifying solar equipment.
The local certification must be transmitted to or filed with the tax assessor so the exemption can be applied for the applicable tax years.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: A qualifying residential solar installation may receive the benefit, but the applicable route depends on system characteristics and local adoption, followed by certification and assessor processing.
reviews.evidenceText: Virginia law provides a local certification-to-assessor process for qualifying solar equipment, while specified small solar installations may qualify under a separate statewide statutory route.

approvalRequirements: A municipality must have established a sustainable-energy program under the current enabling statute and must be accepting applications for the relevant property type.
The property must be qualifying property, and the owner must request the financing and consent to the contractual assessment.
The owner must complete the energy audit or renewable-energy feasibility analysis required before municipal approval.
The project and applicant must pass the municipality's eligibility, financing, assessment, and lien-related review.
The owner and program parties must execute the contractual assessment and financing documents before project funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Connecticut law still authorizes municipal residential sustainable-energy assessment programs, but current official state program sources do not identify a standard active statewide residential PACE offering or a current municipal participation roster.
reviews.evidenceText: Section 7-121n authorizes municipalities to create sustainable-energy assessment programs, but current state program pages do not substantiate a standard active statewide residential PACE application route.

approvalRequirements: The project must be located in a designated Rural Renewable Energy Development Zone and use an eligible renewable-energy technology.
The business and project must satisfy the applicable enterprise-zone investment, use, and employment requirements or obtain any authorized local waiver.
The applicant must obtain local zone preauthorization before beginning construction, installation, or other disqualifying project work.
After the property is placed in service, the owner must file the required exemption claim and supporting records with the county assessor.
The project must maintain continuing statutory and local program compliance during the exemption term.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The active program uses defined zone, technology, investment, and filing criteria. A project that receives timely local preauthorization and meets the enterprise-zone conditions is likely to obtain the stated tax treatment.
reviews.evidenceText: Oregon's active RRED Zone program requires local preauthorization before project work and a later county-assessor claim after qualifying property is placed in service.

approvalRequirements: The purchased property must be a component used in the production of electricity from an eligible renewable-energy source under Colorado's exemption rules.
The applicable city or county must have adopted the local exemption; home-rule local taxes must be checked separately.
The purchaser or seller must retain records substantiating the qualifying component and the taxing jurisdictions involved.
The exemption must be applied at the point of sale or recovered through the applicable tax refund or return process.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: State and certain special-district taxes follow the published component exemption, but city, county, and home-rule treatment varies by local adoption and jurisdiction.
reviews.evidenceText: Colorado's renewable-electricity component exemption applies to state and certain special-district taxes, while city and county treatment depends on local adoption and home-rule taxes are separate.

approvalRequirements: The system must use a currently eligible technology and satisfy the applicable construction, ownership, use, and statutory date requirements.
The relevant taxing jurisdiction must not have opted out of the exemption for the applicable system class.
The owner must comply with any required notice process and any lawfully requested payment-in-lieu-of-taxes agreement.
The owner must file Form RP-487 and the required system, cost, construction, and ownership documentation with the local assessor by the applicable taxable-status date.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The exemption is a statutory, noncompetitive benefit for a qualifying system in a jurisdiction that has not opted out, although local PILOT and assessor procedures still apply.
reviews.evidenceText: Eligible systems receive a 15-year assessment exemption unless the taxing jurisdiction opted out; owners file RP-487 and may be subject to a local PILOT process.

approvalRequirements: The property must be in or be added to a participating special energy improvement district.
The proposed improvement must qualify as a special energy improvement under current Ohio law.
The affected property owner or owners must submit the required petition and consent to the special assessment.
The district plan and project must receive the required municipal or township resolution and other local approvals.
The owner and financing parties must execute the financing, cooperative, and special-assessment documents before funding and installation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: C-PACE projects require an active district, owner petition, local governmental approval, financing terms, and assessment documentation; eligibility alone does not secure financing.
reviews.evidenceText: Ohio law requires an owner petition, a special energy improvement district plan, local resolution approval, and execution of financing and special-assessment documents.

approvalRequirements: The property must be in a municipality that has adopted a C-PACE district, program guide, and application process.
The property must meet the current commercial, industrial, or qualifying multifamily eligibility rules.
The proposed improvement must qualify under the local program and be supported by the required energy audit, feasibility study, resiliency analysis, or other technical documentation.
The owner must submit a voluntary application and pass program-administrator and capital-provider underwriting.
The owner must obtain any required mortgage-holder consent and execute the voluntary assessment and financing agreements before the assessment is recorded.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Nevada authorizes local C-PACE programs and at least one municipality identifies an active pathway, but each project depends on local participation, technical review, underwriting, and assessment-contract approval.
reviews.evidenceText: Nevada law authorizes local C-PACE districts with program guides and voluntary assessment agreements, and Reno currently identifies an active C-PACE program.

approvalRequirements: A city, county, or development authority must have established a commercial property assessed conservation, energy, and resiliency program by the required local action.
The property must be qualifying commercial, industrial, agricultural, or multifamily property with at least five dwelling units.
The proposed permanently affixed improvement must qualify under the program, including an eligible energy, water, conservation, or resiliency measure.
The owner must submit the financing application with the required professional energy, water, new-construction, or resiliency analysis or certification.
The property must satisfy delinquency, debt-to-value, useful-life, and other statutory underwriting requirements.
Every prior lienholder must provide written consent, and the owner and program parties must execute and record the assessment agreement.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Georgia now authorizes local C-PACE programs, but availability and approval depend on local implementation, statutory underwriting, prior-lienholder consent, and financing close.
reviews.evidenceText: Georgia's 2024 C-PACE law authorizes local programs for commercial, industrial, agricultural, and qualifying multifamily properties and includes energy storage among eligible resiliency improvements.

approvalRequirements: The property must be business-owned machinery and tools used directly in producing or generating renewable energy as defined by current Virginia law.
The locality must have adopted a reduced or zero tax rate for the separately classified renewable-energy machinery and tools.
The taxpayer must accurately report and classify the property on the applicable local machinery-and-tools return and retain supporting records.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: State law creates the separate property class, but the actual tax reduction depends on whether the locality adopted a lower or zero rate and accepts the property's classification.
reviews.evidenceText: Virginia separately classifies qualifying business renewable-energy machinery and tools, but each locality decides whether to impose a reduced or zero tax rate.

approvalRequirements: The applicant must be a Lodi Electric Utility commercial or industrial customer on an eligible rate schedule.
The account must satisfy the minimum active-service period and recent payment-history requirements.
The proposed project must qualify for a Lodi Electric Utility energy-efficiency rebate and meet the minimum eligible project-cost threshold after the rebate.
The customer must submit the required energy audit, contractor proposal, project information, and financing application before work proceeds.
The customer must pass utility review and any applicable credit, account, cost, and project verification before on-bill financing is approved.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The utility offers a defined zero-interest on-bill financing route, but approval depends on rate class, account tenure and payment history, rebate qualification, project cost, and utility review.
reviews.evidenceText: Lodi's current on-bill financing requires an eligible business rate class, established service and payment history, an LEU rebate, an audit or proposal, and project review.

approvalRequirements: The applicant must be an eligible Lodi Electric Utility commercial customer for the installation site.
The equipment or project must be listed in the current commercial rebate offering and meet all measure-specific efficiency, installation, and operating requirements.
The customer must obtain preapproval before purchase or installation where the selected measure or custom project requires it.
The customer must submit the current application with invoices, equipment data, contractor information, and other required completion records.
The installation must pass any requested utility inspection or verification and remain within current incentive and project caps.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current program uses published prescriptive or custom criteria rather than competitive ranking. An eligible project that follows any required preapproval and submits complete closeout records is likely to be paid.
reviews.evidenceText: Lodi's current commercial rebates use published equipment criteria, preapproval for specified measures, post-installation documentation, and possible inspection.

approvalRequirements: The applicant must be an eligible Lodi Electric Utility residential customer for the purchase or installation address.
The product or improvement must be currently listed and meet the applicable ENERGY STAR, efficiency, fuel, sizing, installation, and other measure-specific requirements.
The customer must submit the applicable online or written rebate application with proof of purchase, model or certification information, and installation records within the stated claim period.
The customer must allow any requested inspection or verification and comply with current per-customer and funding limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current residential offer uses fixed, measure-specific eligibility and document review. A timely, complete claim for a qualifying product or installation is likely to receive the rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: Lodi's current residential rebates use published product and efficiency criteria with an application, proof of purchase, and inspection or verification where required.

approvalRequirements: The applicant must respond during an open Louisiana Department of Transportation and Development NEVI procurement round.
The proposer and site must satisfy the designated corridor-group, public-access, site-control, and distance-from-corridor requirements in the solicitation.
The project must provide federally compliant DC fast-charging equipment and meet all applicable technical, networking, payment, uptime, accessibility, and procurement requirements.
The proposer must document at least the required 20 percent nonfederal cost share and provide the complete technical, financial, business, and operations proposal.
The proposer must commit to the required long-term operations and maintenance obligations and pass competitive evaluation and contract negotiation before construction.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current official page says DOTD is evaluating updated federal guidance and developing a competitive program; no open current application round was identified, and any future award will require competitive selection.
reviews.evidenceText: DOTD's official materials describe a competitive, corridor-based DC fast-charging program with an 80 percent federal share, a 20 percent recipient match, and long-term operations obligations; no current open round is identified.

approvalRequirements: The participant must have an eligible Louisville Gas and Electric or Kentucky Utilities residential or qualifying small-business electric account.
A compatible internet-connected smart thermostat must be installed and associated with the eligible premises.
The customer must complete the enrollment process, provide required account and device authorizations, and receive program acceptance.
The thermostat must remain connected and enrolled for ongoing event participation and recurring rewards.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: This is a published demand-response enrollment incentive with objective account and device requirements. An eligible customer with a compatible connected thermostat is likely to be accepted and receive rewards while remaining enrolled.
reviews.evidenceText: Eligible LG&E and KU customers with a compatible connected thermostat enroll for utility acceptance and ongoing demand-response participation and rewards.

approvalRequirements: The participant must have an eligible LG&E or KU residential or qualifying small-commercial account and rate.
The customer must have a compatible connected electric vehicle or eligible Level 2 smart charging station in operation at the account location.
The customer must complete enrollment, provide account, vehicle or charger, data-access, and control authorizations, and receive program acceptance.
The enrolled vehicle or charger must remain connected and participating under the optimized-charging terms for recurring rewards.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current offer uses objective account, vehicle or charger, connectivity, and enrollment requirements rather than competitive selection. A compatible accepted enrollment is likely to receive the published rewards.
reviews.evidenceText: Eligible LG&E and KU residential and small-commercial customers can enroll a compatible connected EV or Level 2 charger for optimized charging and ongoing rewards.

approvalRequirements: The business must have an active eligible LG&E or KU account on a qualifying General Service or applicable commercial gas rate.
The applicant must own or operate a qualifying small business at the serviced premises.
The premises must not have received the same audit and direct-install service within the current three-year participation interval.
The customer must enroll, provide access and relevant facility information, and coordinate the scheduled audit and installation visit.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The audit and basic measures are a no-cost utility service with objective account and participation rules. An eligible small business that enrolls and accommodates the visit is likely to receive the service.
reviews.evidenceText: Eligible General Service small-business customers can enroll for a no-cost audit and basic efficiency measures, subject to account and three-year participation rules.

approvalRequirements: The apartment owner must have an eligible LG&E or KU residential or General Service common-area account with the minimum service history.
The building must contain at least four dwelling units and satisfy the program's tenant income or qualifying-assistance participation threshold.
The property must satisfy the current address-level participation interval and other program eligibility rules.
The owner must enroll, provide required tenant notices and access, supply eligibility information, and permit the audit and installation work.
Any whole-building project incentive must receive the required project review and comply with the current eligible-cost and owner-contribution terms.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: WeCare uses defined account, building-size, income, access, and participation rules. An owner who documents eligibility and permits the assessment is likely to receive the audit and approved measures.
reviews.evidenceText: WeCare screens the utility account, apartment-building size, tenant income-program participation, prior service history, and property access before providing audits and measures.

approvalRequirements: The applicant must have an eligible LG&E or KU residential account with the minimum required service history.
The dwelling must be an eligible home or building with fewer than four units and must satisfy the address-level participation interval.
The household must meet the current income limit or qualifying-assistance-program criteria and complete the required self-attestation or documentation.
A renter must obtain the property owner's consent where the proposed work requires it.
The participant must enroll, permit the home audit, and provide access for approved direct-install or weatherization measures.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current program uses objective account, home, participation-history, income, and access rules. A qualifying household that completes enrollment and the audit is likely to receive approved no-cost measures.
reviews.evidenceText: WeCare screens account tenure, dwelling type, prior participation, household income eligibility, and landlord consent where applicable before the home audit and measures.

approvalRequirements: The applicant must be a City of Loveland Utilities residential electric customer at an eligible existing dwelling.
The selected measure must be listed in the current Loveland or Efficiency Works residential offering and meet all technical, product, and installation specifications.
For measures that require it, the customer must complete a home assessment before work and use an Efficiency Works qualified service provider.

The project must be submitted through the required provider pathway or the customer must file the post-purchase application with invoices, receipts, model data, and other records within the stated deadline.
The installation must pass any required inspection or verification and remain within current funding and incentive limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current program has prescriptive measure and documentation rules. A qualifying customer who follows the required assessment or provider pathway and files on time is likely to receive the rebate while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Loveland residential rebates require utility eligibility, measure-specific criteria, pre-work assessment or qualified-provider submission for many projects, and timely post-purchase filing.
